answer: Cross-Epoch Behavioural Anchor (CEBA): each agent earns routing weight only by matching a rolling 3-epoch behavioral fingerprint—latency quantiles, tool-call transition graph, error signatures—computed on shale-like noisy tasks during a calibration voyage. A Mahalanobis deviation above threshold throttles the agent until it re-anchors across two epochs. Attackers must run every Sybil through this multi-epoch voyage, paying sustained compute, latency noise, and correlation risk from shared infrastructure; fresh identities cannot be minted cheaply.
